page: Microsoft Azure A1_v2 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the Av2 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single dedicated x86_64 vCPU mapped to one physical core and one thread, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8171M processor operating at 2.6 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.25 MB of L2 cache, and 50 MB of L3 cache. System memory is limited to 2.0 GB of RAM, and the instance is bundled with 10 GB of local storage. No complimentary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results place the A1_v2 consistently in the bottom 10% of performance categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both score 331.25. Memory bandwidth is constrained, with read-only small block cached memory at 28.82 GB/sec, dropping to 3.72 GB/sec for large block uncached reads, and 3.18 GB/sec for large block writes. Passmark CPU and memory scores are 425.99 and 393.63 respectively. Cryptographic and compression tasks are also limited, with a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 108.34 and single-threaded gzip compression at 6.68 GB/sec.

Due to its low resource density and poor benchmark-relative performance, the A1_v2 represents a low-cost entry point for non-demanding tasks rather than high-throughput workloads. Redis SET operations achieve 0.45 million operations per second, and static web serving throughput is limited to 0.45 GB/sec. Small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model yields 31.53 tokens per second for prompt processing and 12.39 tokens per second for text generation. This server is best suited for basic development environments, low-traffic testing, or lightweight background processes that do not require significant memory or compute power.
